prompt.en: Pure economic systems rarely exist in real life. Examine the limitations of a purely planned and a purely market economy, and explain why a mixed economy is often seen as more practical. (5 marks)

label.en: Planned economies have few rivals, so little push to improve or innovate

level1.en: If the plan fixes a factory's target and price, what reason does it have to improve?

clue.en: Remember the planned umbrellas: when buyers wanted more, nothing changed until the next plan.

level2Template.en: In a planned economy, firms follow targets and have few rivals, so there is little push to improve quality or ___.

label.en: Pure markets provide too few public goods

level1.en: Which useful things does no private seller provide, because nobody can be made to pay for each use?

clue.en: Remember the street light: everyone walking by uses it, and no seller can charge them.

level2Template.en: Private sellers cannot charge each user for ___, such as street lights and roads, so a pure market economy provides too few of them.

label.en: Almost all real economies are mixed, even market ones

level1.en: Does the book name any market economy where the government plays no part?

clue.en: The book says even the USA and Singapore have significant government involvement in the market.

level2Template.en: Almost all real economies are ___: even market economies such as the USA and Singapore have a lot of government involvement.

label.en: A mixed economy combines what each side does well

level1.en: What does each side bring to a mixed economy?

clue.en: The government side: fair rules, consumer protection, public goods, welfare. The market side: profit-making firms, competition, new ideas.

level2Template.en: A mixed economy combines government rules, public goods and welfare with private firms, competition and ___.

label.en: The mix can change over time, as India's did after 1991

level1.en: Did India give up the government's role in 1991? What changed?

clue.en: The reforms cut excessive rules and let in more private firms and competition, but the government kept an important role.

level2Template.en: After 1991, India moved towards a more market-oriented system while keeping an important role for the ___.

text.en: Pure economic systems are rare, and each one has limitations.
In a planned economy, firms follow targets and have few rivals, so there is little push to improve quality or ___.
Private sellers cannot charge each user for ___, such as street lights and roads, so a pure market economy provides too few of them.
Almost all real economies are ___: even market economies such as the USA and Singapore have a lot of government involvement.
A mixed economy combines government rules, public goods and welfare with private firms, competition and ___.
After 1991, India moved towards a more market-oriented system while keeping an important role for the ___.
